children: U.K. inflation data and jobs data released this week showed little evidence of second-round inflation effects, which could enable the Bank of England to raise rates gradually, Mizuho's Evelyne Gomez-Liechti says in a note. The jobs data showed a fairly stable labor market with no evidence of acceleration in wage growth, while U.K. annual services inflation data for October came in at 3.7%, undershooting the BOE forecast of 3.9%. The jobs and inflation data can buy the BOE some time if it prefers to proceed more gradually than markets currently price in, Gomez-Liechti says. Investors price in an additional three BOE rate increases by mid-2027, in addition to the rate increase delivered in November, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
